lead.headline: Gunmen fire at Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff's car in Juhu; he survives, and three suspects are held in Rajasthan
lead.short: At least two men fired several shots at close range into the front passenger seat of actor Tiger Shroff's car on Sunday evening as it left a football ground in Mumbai's Juhu. Shroff, 36, was not hit by a bullet, police said, but two people, including his driver, were injured. Three suspects were detained in Rajasthan on Monday.

why.text: Mumbai has seen several actors and politicians targeted by gunmen in recent years, and this attack came in a crowded street.

more: Videos showed the car moving slowly past a crowd when the men opened fire. Shroff, the son of actor Jackie Shroff, plays football for Mumbay FC and was leaving his regular practice. Photographs showed him with bandages on his upper body; the extent of his injuries is not clear.
Rajasthan police said two of the three detained men were from Haryana and Bihar and had lived in Mumbai for some years. The third is a minor. They were to be handed to Mumbai Police on Monday.

Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Shroff and said he was "shaken". "These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated," Shinde said. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis called the attack "serious and condemnable" and promised the actor "complete safety".

seconds.headline: Rubio says an India-US trade deal is 'very close' and helped decide the Russia waiver, before meeting Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday
seconds.short: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that the US is "very close" to finalising a trade deal with India, and that this was one of the things Washington weighed in waiving the Russia oil sanctions. He meets External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday 20 October, the foreign ministry has said.

why.text: With the 100% tariff threat lifted, the last big difference between the two countries over a trade deal is out of the way.

more: "We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that," Rubio told a press conference in Uzbekistan. "You also can't unravel the economy of other countries because of one central issue," he said, adding that some countries find it very hard to buy energy elsewhere.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told NBC that Washington had asked European allies in the spring to put secondary tariffs on India and China for buying Russian oil. "They refused. So why should the US bear the burden?" he said, adding that 136 of 140 cargoes from Russia's Yamal gas plant in the first half of the year went to Europe.
The waiver gives the administration 60 days to assess the sanctions law's effects.

update.new: Rubio says the trade deal is very close; the Mumbai talks are on Tuesday 20 October.
update.front: Washington now says a trade deal with India is within reach, the day before its top diplomat meets Jaishankar.

seconds.headline: The Sensex falls 1.2% by 2pm as HDFC Bank, ICICI and Axis slide after their results and foreign investors keep selling
seconds.short: The Sensex was down 925 points, or 1.2%, at 73,804 at 2pm on Monday, and the Nifty had slipped below 23,000 to 22,878. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank were the biggest drags after reporting their September-quarter results, Business Standard reported, with foreign selling and high oil prices adding to the pressure.

why.text: Private banks are the heaviest weights in both indices, so their fall pulled down savings parked in index funds.

more: HDFC Bank fell about 2% in early trade after its profit rose only 5% and brokerages flagged pressure on its interest margins; JPMorgan cut its target to ₹970. Fewer than 100 of the 500 biggest listed companies were up. The India VIX, a gauge of expected volatility, rose more than 5%.

State-run banks went the other way: Union Bank of India rose 5.2% and Punjab National Bank 5%. Brent crude eased 2.3% to $107.38 a barrel on expectations that Trump's Russia waiver will free more supply, but stayed near its highest in months.
Bernstein cut its December target for the Nifty to 25,000 from 26,000 on Monday, citing crude, supply-chain pressure and few earnings upgrades.

facts.drags: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank

seconds.headline: Anthropic puts 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund, rising to about 20% as it grows, and Musk says give them away directly
seconds.short: Anthropic said it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, subject to shareholder approval, with up to 2% more for every 50% rise in the company's value over a set baseline. In total, it said, roughly 20% of its shares are now committed to the public good.

why.text: It sets aside a large slice of one of the most valuable AI companies for public causes before its expected stock market listing.

more: The fund is a wholly owned entity with more flexibility than the company itself, Anthropic said, and could make large donations to charities or pay money directly to specific groups of people. It named the effect of AI on jobs as one example: it has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing it.
Its co-founders have pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and about half its staff give part of theirs through a matching programme the company has run since it was founded.

Elon Musk replied on X: "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public." In a second post he added: "This is what I will be doing." Anthropic is a public benefit corporation and does most of its mission work, such as safety research, inside the company.

seconds.headline: Macron says looters will pay and vows to hold accountable those who 'sought to bring down the Republic' as arrests reach 2,400
seconds.short: President Emmanuel Macron said on Sunday that those who looted during Saturday's protests would have to pay for the damage, and blamed "insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals". At least 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend. He refused the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

why.text: The arrests are close to the record set in a single day of the yellow vest protests in 2018.

more: In a televised address, Macron said he had told prefects to work with mayors to protect public buildings and businesses in the coming weeks, including by banning protests when necessary. Marseille has banned public gatherings. Hundreds gathered again at Place de la République in Paris on Sunday, where police used tear gas.

"The right to protest is a fundamental right. Deliberately and collectively sowing disorder through violence is not," Nuñez wrote on X, citing the looting of hundreds of businesses. Macron said he should stay to keep the chain of command with the police.
Officials estimated Saturday's turnout at 550,000 and organisers at 800,000. Paris police said one person died of a heart attack. Limoges's 19th-century city hall was nearly destroyed.

update.new: Macron addressed the nation and blamed the far left; arrests rose to 2,400.
update.front: The president has now spoken, promising prosecutions and possible protest bans, as arrests doubled.

briefs.headline: Seven held over the Kolkata Durga Puja crush are sent to police custody for 10 days, as the toll reaches 19
briefs.text: The Trinamool Congress asked why the state had named the Chorbagan Sarbojonin puja "Best of the Best", with prizes for its lighting and pandal, after the chief minister blamed its theme and low lighting for the crush. Twenty-five people were injured.

update.new: Toll at 19; seven accused in 10-day custody.

briefs.headline: Discharged: L.K. Advani leaves Apollo Hospital in Delhi after recovering from a chest infection
briefs.text: The 98-year-old former deputy prime minister had been admitted on 16 October with a chest infection and pulmonary complications. The hospital said on Monday that his condition had improved.

stories.headline: Canada names the four soldiers killed in the Wainwright base fire, fewer than first reported, with 19 of 39 injured in critical condition
stories.short: Four Canadian soldiers died in Saturday's fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, officials confirmed, after earlier media reports put the toll at seven. Of 39 people in hospital, at least 19 are critical, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said. Prime Minister Mark Carney called it "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime".

why.text: The army is investigating how a training-ground grass fire reached troops on a live-fire range.

more: The BBC confirmed the dead as Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark. The fire is now contained.

Infantry had been doing "high-intensity combat training with live munitions" at a grenade range and an attack range, Maj-Gen Wade Rutland said, with grenades, a grenade launcher and small arms in use. A grass fire started about 1km away, cause still under investigation, and "uncommonly strong winds caused the fire to spread rapidly and shift direction towards the range administrative area".
"The nation is in mourning," Carney said in an address from Ottawa, adding that crews fought the flames all night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".

update.new: Officials confirmed four dead, not the seven first reported, and named them.

update.new: Police made arrests; the Guardian published video of the attackers.

briefs.text: Apple first planned to launch only in the US and China, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman wrote, but opened orders in more than 70 countries despite knowing of severe supply limits. Estimates moved to about 25 January within 30 minutes.

briefs.text: After a 10-month cruise, MMX is to spend about three years at Phobos, land a rover and scoop samples, then fly past Deimos and leave in November 2030. The capsule is due to land in Australia in 2031.

briefs.text: It was only Madueke's second Premier League start of the season, and his goal kept Arsenal's title defence on track. Christos Tzolis, signed to replace Leandro Trossard, has been Mikel Arteta's first-choice left winger.

update.new: Arsenal won 1–0 at Forest on Saturday.

briefs.headline: Manchester United draw 1–1 at Leeds and have seven points from seven games, but Carrick calls it 'a fresh start'
briefs.text: United have won once in the league this season and lost 2–0 at Atlético Madrid in midweek, after which Lisandro Martínez criticised the club's recruitment. "The headphones have been on this week," Michael Carrick said.

stories.headline: Mbappé scores twice as Madrid beat Sevilla 4–1 without Vinícius and stay six points behind Barcelona before the Clásico
stories.short: Real Madrid beat Sevilla 4–1 at the Bernabéu on Sunday. Arda Güler opened the scoring after 30 minutes, Kylian Mbappé added two, one a penalty, and Yan Diomande hit a late fourth. Manu Bueno replied for Sevilla. Madrid stay six points behind leaders Barcelona, whom they visit on Sunday 25 October.

why.text: Madrid won comfortably in the first game of Vinícius's ban, which also rules him out of the Clásico.

more: Mbappé's first came seven minutes after Güler's strike, when he rounded goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos. He was then brought down in the box and scored the penalty himself, taking him to 11 goals in 11 games this season.

Diomande, in Vinícius's place, set up Güler's opener and led the match with 11 progressive carries and 35 touches in the final third. Dean Huijsen had the most touches on the pitch, 105, and completed 96.8% of his passes. Güler made three key passes in his 77 minutes, before a sending-off that drew comment in Italy and Spain.
Madrid host RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday, three days after Leipzig lost 6–1 at Bayern.

stories.headline: Mona Agarwal beats Avani Lekhara by 0.4 points on the last shot as India take gold and silver on the Asian Para Games' first day
stories.short: Mona Agarwal came from sixth place in the final to win the women's 10m air rifle SH1 gold at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya on Monday, setting a Games record of 250.0. Avani Lekhara, the defending champion and two-time Paralympic gold medallist, took silver with 249.6. South Korea's Yunri Lee won bronze.

why.text: India opened its medal account with a one-two, and Avani's silver earned a second quota place for the 2028 Paralympics.

more: The duel between the two shooters from Jaipur went down to the last of 24 shots. Avani led 239.2 to 239.1 before the final shot, and Mona finished stronger.

Mona won bronze at the 2024 Paris Paralympics and silver at the World Shooting Para Sport championships in Changwon, South Korea, last month, where she earned India's first quota place in the event for Los Angeles. SH1 is the class for shooters with lower-limb impairments.

More than 150 Indian athletes are in Japan, and the contingent is aiming for more than 100 medals. Sprinter Simran Sharma and shuttler Pramod Bhagat carried the flag at the opening ceremony. In para badminton, Manasi Joshi and Thulasimathi Murugesan reached the semi-finals, assuring India of a medal.

briefs.headline: Barcelona visit Luis Enrique's PSG at the Parc des Princes on Wednesday, nine years after the 6–1 comeback he called the greatest ever
briefs.text: Enrique managed Barcelona that night and now coaches PSG. Barcelona arrive after a 5–2 win at Real Betis that kept their perfect league record.

briefs.headline: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina comes from a set and a break down to beat Rafael Jodar for his first Masters title, in Shanghai
briefs.text: He won 1-6 7-6 (5) 6-4, after also coming back to beat Alexander Zverev in the semi-final. Davidovich Fokina lost his first five career finals and has now won all three he has played this year.

briefs.headline: Chwalinska comes from a set down to beat Kartal 2-6 6-4 6-2 for her first WTA title, in Wuhan
briefs.text: The final lasted 2 hours 43 minutes. Kartal, ranked 170th before the week, earned 650 ranking points and $385,001, and will be Britain's number one when the rankings come out.

update.new: Kartal lost the final in three sets.
